title: Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMPLE POEMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we repeat some sounds, words and lines in a poem?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem
2. describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem
   In simple words: practise until you can identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem
   In simple words: practise until you can describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
4. Show that you can: identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read provided simple poems individually and in groups,
2. Self-efficacy: It is nurtured as the learner recites poems.
3. Learning to learn: It is encouraged as the learner builds on their own learning when studying on their own.
4. Communication and collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner reads and recites poems. Values:
5. Unity: It is cultivated as the learner collaborates with others to recite poems.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify basic aspects of style such as repetition and rhyme in a poem
2. describe the functions of rhyme and repetition in a poem

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
